resources.string: Chinese-only recognition; fast and accurate. The right choice when you only need subtitles for Chinese audio.
Japanese-only recognition; Chinese and English are not supported. Decodes whole segments, which is more accurate for Japanese than the streaming model.
Handles sentences that mix Chinese and English; English words are kept as they are. A larger model, and slower to run.
The download source URL is invalid: %1$s
This file has no usable audio track

This file (or stream) declares no duration, so it cannot be split into 5-minute chunks for upload. Use on-device recognition instead — it decodes and recognizes as it goes and does not need the duration up front.
The subtitles were generated but could not be saved (storage may be full)
Official OpenAI. The default whisper-1 is the only model here that reliably returns per-sentence timestamps; switching to gpt-4o-transcribe collapses the subtitles into one block.
Keep the /openai/v1 segment in the address — that is the path the official SDK uses, and removing it returns 404. The only model names are whisper-large-v3 and whisper-large-v3-turbo.

This provider does not return timestamps: the whole audio becomes one block of text, i.e. a single subtitle line. Directly reachable in mainland China and cheap — good when all you want is a transcript.

Enter an OpenAI-compatible base (e.g. https://example.com/v1); the resolved request URL is shown below. It requests timestamps by default — if the provider rejects that, you will be told to switch model or preset.
Fill in only if the provider requires it
%1$s rejected the request — the API key is missing or wrong. Fix it in Settings → Speech recognition and try again.
The provider rejected the request by account policy: %1$s (retyping the key will not help — you likely need a different provider)
The provider will not accept this request: %1$s. The usual cause is that the model does not support returning timestamps — try another model or preset.
This audio chunk (%1$s) exceeds the provider size limit. On-device recognition uploads nothing and has no such limit.
Could not read what the provider returned: %1$s
There is no transcription endpoint at this address (HTTP %1$d). Check the service address in Settings → Speech recognition — most OpenAI-compatible services need the path to include /v1.

The cloud recognition service address is not filled in properly — it must start with http:// or https://. Complete it in Settings → Speech recognition → Cloud recognition, or switch back to on-device recognition.
